symptoms: Uniform green color, no spots, no wilting, normal leaf shape and size.
cause: Not applicable - crop is healthy.
favorable_weather: Any normal seasonal weather with balanced irrigation and nutrition.
organic_control: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring and good crop practices.
chemical_control: Not applicable.
cultural_practice: Continue routine irrigation, balanced fertilization and periodic scouting.
prevention: Maintain balanced nutrition, proper spacing and regular field sanitation.
dosage_note: Not applicable.
expert_escalation_condition: Not applicable - no issue detected.

symptoms: White to greyish powdery coating on the upper leaf surface, leaves may curl and yellow over time.
cause: Fungal infection (Phyllactinia/Uncinula species) favored by high humidity with moderate temperatures.
favorable_weather: Warm days, cool humid nights, poor air circulation in dense canopy.
organic_control: Spray neem oil solution (approx. 5 ml/litre water) every 7-10 days; dust wettable sulfur in early morning.
chemical_control: Sulfur-based or triazole fungicides as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Improve canopy airflow via pruning; avoid excess nitrogen which promotes tender, susceptible growth.
prevention: Maintain plant spacing, avoid overhead irrigation late in the day, remove heavily infected leaves.
dosage_note: Follow product label; typical neem oil 5 ml/litre + mild soap as spreader.
expert_escalation_condition: If more than 40% of the plot canopy is affected or mildew persists after 2 spray cycles.

symptoms: Small brown to black circular spots scattered across the leaf, sometimes with yellow halos.
cause: Fungal pathogens thriving in prolonged leaf wetness and high humidity.
favorable_weather: Frequent rain, high humidity, poor drainage.
organic_control: Remove and destroy affected leaves; apply neem-based fungicidal spray at first sign.
chemical_control: Copper-oxychloride based fungicide as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Avoid overhead irrigation, ensure field drainage, remove leaf litter.
prevention: Balanced fertilization, timely pruning for airflow, crop rotation for nursery beds.
dosage_note: Copper oxychloride typically 2-3 g/litre - confirm with local label.
expert_escalation_condition: If spots spread rapidly across new leaves within a week of treatment.

symptoms: Orange-brown pustules on the underside of leaves, yellowing of upper surface.
cause: Rust fungus favored by high humidity and cooler night temperatures.
favorable_weather: High humidity (>80%), cooler nights, dew formation.
organic_control: Remove infected leaves promptly; neem oil spray at early pustule stage.
chemical_control: Triazole/strobilurin fungicide as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Avoid dense planting; ensure good sunlight penetration into canopy.
prevention: Field sanitation, avoid late evening irrigation, monitor during humid spells.
dosage_note: Follow product label instructions strictly.
expert_escalation_condition: If pustules appear on more than half the plot or spread to new shoots.

symptoms: Water-soaked angular spots turning dark brown/black, may have a yellow halo; leaves may tear.
cause: Bacterial infection spread by rain splash and contaminated tools.
favorable_weather: Warm, wet, humid conditions with frequent rain.
organic_control: Remove infected leaves; avoid working in wet fields; copper-based organic bactericide spray.
chemical_control: Copper-based bactericide as locally recommended - no reliable curative chemical exists once established.
cultural_practice: Disinfect pruning tools between plants; avoid overhead irrigation.
prevention: Use disease-free planting material; avoid field work during/after rain.
dosage_note: Copper-based products per label - confirm with local agriculture office.
expert_escalation_condition: Bacterial diseases spread fast in wet weather - escalate if not contained within 1-2 weeks.

symptoms: Grey-centered circular spots with dark brown margins, often merging into larger patches.
cause: Cercospora fungus favored by warm, humid, wet conditions.
favorable_weather: Warm temperature with high humidity and leaf wetness.
organic_control: Remove affected leaves; neem-based spray at early stage.
chemical_control: Mancozeb-based fungicide as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Avoid excess nitrogen; maintain plant spacing for airflow.
prevention: Field sanitation, resistant variety selection where available.
dosage_note: Mancozeb typically 2-2.5 g/litre - confirm with local label.
expert_escalation_condition: If spots merge and cause significant defoliation.

symptoms: Irregular brown lesions, sometimes with concentric rings and black fungal fruiting bodies.
cause: Myrothecium fungus, often entering through wounds, favored by wet foliage.
favorable_weather: Prolonged wet, humid conditions with injured leaf tissue.
organic_control: Remove and destroy affected debris; avoid mechanical injury during harvest.
chemical_control: Broad-spectrum fungicide as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Handle leaves carefully during harvest to avoid wounds; clear field debris.
prevention: Avoid harvesting in wet conditions; sanitize tools.
dosage_note: Follow product label instructions strictly.
expert_escalation_condition: If lesions increase rapidly after leaf harvest cycles.

symptoms: Large, irregular brown/necrotic patches, often starting at leaf tips or margins, rapid drying.
cause: Fungal pathogens spreading rapidly in warm, wet, humid weather.
favorable_weather: Extended rain, warm temperatures, poor drainage.
organic_control: Remove severely affected leaves; neem-based spray at first sign.
chemical_control: Broad-spectrum fungicide as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Improve field drainage; avoid excess irrigation.
prevention: Field sanitation, balanced fertilization, timely pruning.
dosage_note: Follow product label instructions strictly.
expert_escalation_condition: If blight spreads to more than 30% of plot within a few days.

symptoms: Wilting despite adequate soil moisture, yellowing leaves, stunted growth, soft dark roots on inspection.
cause: Soil-borne fungi favored by waterlogging and poor drainage.
favorable_weather: Excess soil moisture, waterlogged or poorly drained soil.
organic_control: Improve drainage immediately; apply Trichoderma-based biofungicide to soil.
chemical_control: Systemic fungicide soil drench as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Avoid overwatering; raise planting beds in low-lying plots.
prevention: Ensure good field drainage before planting; avoid waterlogging.
dosage_note: Trichoderma typically applied as soil drench per product label.
expert_escalation_condition: Root rot often requires expert soil diagnosis - escalate promptly if plants are wilting/dying.

symptoms: Sunken, discolored lesions on stem/branch bark, sometimes with cracking or gum exudation.
cause: Fungal infection entering through wounds or pruning cuts, worsened by stress.
favorable_weather: Wet weather following pruning or physical injury.
organic_control: Prune out and destroy affected branches well below the lesion; apply Bordeaux paste to cuts.
chemical_control: Copper-based wound dressing/fungicide as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Prune in dry weather; disinfect tools between plants.
prevention: Avoid unnecessary wounding; maintain plant vigor with balanced nutrition.
dosage_note: Bordeaux paste prepared per standard 1:1:10 copper sulfate:lime:water ratio - confirm locally.
expert_escalation_condition: If canker girdles the stem or spreads to the main trunk.

symptoms: Stunted growth, yellowing, wilting in patches, small knots/galls visible on roots when inspected.
cause: Root-knot nematodes infesting soil, worse in sandy soils with continuous monoculture.
favorable_weather: Warm soil temperatures, sandy well-drained soils.
organic_control: Apply neem cake to soil; use marigold or other trap/rotation crops between cycles.
chemical_control: Nematicide application as locally recommended by agriculture officer.
cultural_practice: Crop rotation, soil solarization before replanting nursery beds.
prevention: Use nematode-free planting material; avoid continuous mulberry monoculture in infested soil.
dosage_note: Neem cake typically 200-250 kg/acre soil application - confirm locally.
expert_escalation_condition: Confirm via soil/root lab test before large-scale nematicide use.

symptoms: White cottony masses on stems/leaf axils, sticky honeydew, sooty mold, stunted new growth.
cause: Mealybug infestation, spreads via ants and wind, favored by hot dry weather.
favorable_weather: Hot, dry conditions with low rainfall.
organic_control: Spray neem oil (5 ml/litre) with mild soap; introduce natural predators like ladybird beetles.
chemical_control: Systemic insecticide as locally recommended if infestation is severe.
cultural_practice: Remove heavily infested shoots; control ant populations that protect mealybugs.
prevention: Regular scouting of leaf axils and new shoots, avoid excess nitrogen.
dosage_note: Neem oil 5 ml/litre + soap 1 g/litre as spreader.
expert_escalation_condition: If infestation covers multiple plants and honeydew/sooty mold is extensive.

symptoms: Tiny white insects flying up when leaves are disturbed, yellowing leaves, sticky honeydew, sooty mold.
cause: Whitefly infestation favored by warm weather and dense, tender foliage.
favorable_weather: Warm, dry to moderately humid conditions.
organic_control: Yellow sticky traps; neem oil spray (5 ml/litre) targeting the underside of leaves.
chemical_control: Systemic/contact insecticide as locally recommended for severe infestation.
cultural_practice: Remove heavily infested older leaves; avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.
prevention: Regular monitoring of leaf undersides, yellow sticky traps for early detection.
dosage_note: Neem oil 5 ml/litre, spray targeting undersides of leaves in the evening.
expert_escalation_condition: If whitefly is also vectoring visible viral symptoms (mosaic/curling).

symptoms: Silvery streaks or scarring on leaf surface, curled/distorted young leaves, tiny slender insects visible.
cause: Thrips infestation favored by hot, dry weather.
favorable_weather: Hot, dry conditions with low humidity.
organic_control: Blue/yellow sticky traps; neem oil spray at early infestation.
chemical_control: Spinosad or recommended insecticide for severe infestation.
cultural_practice: Maintain field moisture to discourage thrips buildup; remove weeds that host thrips.
prevention: Regular scouting of new shoots, sticky trap monitoring.
dosage_note: Neem oil 5 ml/litre, repeat every 5-7 days during outbreak.
expert_escalation_condition: If new shoot distortion continues despite two treatment cycles.

symptoms: Small brown/grey immobile bumps on stems and leaf undersides, yellowing and weakening of branches.
cause: Scale insect infestation, often spread by ants, favored by dusty/dry conditions.
favorable_weather: Dry, dusty conditions with reduced rainfall.
organic_control: Scrub off visible scales manually on light infestations; horticultural neem oil spray.
chemical_control: Systemic insecticide for heavy infestation as locally recommended.
cultural_practice: Prune and destroy heavily infested branches; manage ant populations.
prevention: Regular stem inspection, avoid water stress which weakens plant defenses.
dosage_note: Neem oil 5 ml/litre, ensure thorough coverage of stems.
expert_escalation_condition: If scale spreads to main stem/trunk affecting overall plant vigor.

symptoms: Fine stippling/bronzing on leaves, fine webbing on underside in heavy infestation, leaf curling.
cause: Mite infestation favored by hot, dry weather and dusty conditions.
favorable_weather: Hot, dry weather with low humidity.
organic_control: Spray water to increase humidity and dislodge mites; neem oil or sulfur-based miticide.
chemical_control: Miticide (acaricide) as locally recommended for severe infestation.
cultural_practice: Avoid water stress; dust control on field paths.
prevention: Regular leaf underside inspection especially in hot dry spells.
dosage_note: Follow acaricide label strictly; rotate products to avoid resistance.
expert_escalation_condition: If bronzing/webbing covers majority of the canopy.

symptoms: Leaves rolled/folded and webbed together, chewed leaf margins, visible caterpillars inside rolled leaves.
cause: Caterpillar/leaf-roller larvae feeding and sheltering inside folded leaves.
favorable_weather: Warm, humid conditions favoring moth activity and egg-laying.
organic_control: Hand-pick and destroy rolled leaves with larvae; Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) based spray.
chemical_control: Recommended larvicide for severe infestation - avoid broad-spectrum sprays near silkworm rearing areas.
cultural_practice: Regular field scouting and manual removal; encourage natural parasitoids.
prevention: Pheromone traps for early moth detection, field sanitation after harvest.
dosage_note: Bt-based product per label, typically applied in the evening.
expert_escalation_condition: IMPORTANT: leaves feeding silkworms must never carry chemical residue - always consult a sericulture expert before spraying near feeding-stage leaf.

symptoms: Uniform yellowing starting from older/lower leaves, stunted growth, thin stems.
cause: Insufficient nitrogen availability in soil, often after heavy leaf harvest cycles.
favorable_weather: Not weather-driven; worsened by leaching after heavy rainfall.
organic_control: Apply well-decomposed FYM/compost, vermicompost, or neem cake as nitrogen source.
chemical_control: Urea or recommended nitrogenous fertilizer per soil-test-based dose.
cultural_practice: Split fertilizer doses aligned with harvest cycles; incorporate green manure crops.
prevention: Follow soil-test-based NPK schedule; avoid over-harvesting leaves without replenishing nutrients.
dosage_note: Follow soil health card recommendation; avoid excess urea which can increase pest susceptibility.
expert_escalation_condition: If yellowing persists despite fertilization - may indicate root or soil health issue.

symptoms: Yellowing/browning at leaf margins (scorch), older leaves affected first, weak stems.
cause: Low soil potassium, often in sandy soils with high rainfall leaching.
favorable_weather: Worsened by high rainfall/leaching in sandy soils.
organic_control: Apply wood ash or potassium-rich compost in moderation.
chemical_control: Muriate of Potash (MOP) or Sulphate of Potash per soil-test-based dose.
cultural_practice: Split potash application across the season; mulch to reduce leaching.
prevention: Periodic soil testing and balanced NPK application.
dosage_note: Follow soil health card recommendation for MOP/SOP dose.
expert_escalation_condition: If margin scorch worsens rapidly across the plot.

symptoms: Interveinal yellowing (veins stay green) on older leaves, sometimes reddish-purple tint.
cause: Low soil magnesium, often aggravated by excess potassium application.
favorable_weather: Not weather-driven; worsened in acidic, sandy soils.
organic_control: Apply organic matter/compost; foliar spray of diluted Epsom salt solution.
chemical_control: Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) foliar spray or soil application per recommendation.
cultural_practice: Balance potassium application which can suppress magnesium uptake.
prevention: Soil testing to catch magnesium levels before visible deficiency appears.
dosage_note: Epsom salt foliar spray typically 5-10 g/litre - confirm with local recommendation.
expert_escalation_condition: If interveinal yellowing spreads to younger leaves too.

symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on young/new leaves specifically (veins stay green, rest turns pale yellow).
cause: Low iron availability, common in alkaline/high-pH soils where iron becomes less soluble.
favorable_weather: Not weather-driven; worsened in high-pH, waterlogged soils.
organic_control: Apply well-decomposed organic matter to gradually lower soil pH and improve iron availability.
chemical_control: Foliar spray of iron chelate (Fe-EDTA) per recommended dose.
cultural_practice: Improve soil drainage; avoid over-liming which raises pH further.
prevention: Periodic soil pH testing, especially in alkaline soil zones.
dosage_note: Fe-EDTA foliar spray typically 2-3 g/litre - confirm with local recommendation.
expert_escalation_condition: If chlorosis affects most new growth despite correction attempts.

symptoms: Small, narrow leaves (little-leaf symptom), interveinal chlorosis, shortened internodes.
cause: Low soil zinc availability, common in high-pH or heavily eroded soils.
favorable_weather: Not weather-driven; worsened in alkaline, low organic matter soils.
organic_control: Apply organic compost regularly to improve micronutrient availability.
chemical_control: Zinc sulfate foliar spray or soil application per recommended dose.
cultural_practice: Avoid excess phosphorus fertilization which can worsen zinc uptake.
prevention: Include micronutrient schedule in annual fertilization plan.
dosage_note: Zinc sulfate foliar spray typically 2-5 g/litre - confirm with local recommendation.
expert_escalation_condition: If little-leaf symptom persists across multiple flush cycles.

symptoms: Wilting/drooping leaves especially in afternoon heat, leaf curling, reduced leaf size, premature leaf drop.
cause: Insufficient soil moisture due to inadequate/irregular irrigation or prolonged dry spell.
favorable_weather: Hot, dry weather with delayed irrigation.
organic_control: Mulch around root zone to conserve soil moisture.
chemical_control: Not applicable - primarily an irrigation management issue.
cultural_practice: Establish a consistent irrigation schedule matched to soil type and season.
prevention: Install drip irrigation where feasible; monitor soil moisture regularly.
dosage_note: Not applicable.
expert_escalation_condition: If wilting persists even after irrigation - check for root damage/disease instead.

symptoms: Bleached/brown patches on leaves exposed directly to intense midday sun, usually on upper canopy.
cause: Intense direct sunlight combined with high temperature and low humidity, often after sudden canopy opening (e.g. after heavy pruning).
favorable_weather: Very hot, sunny days, especially after recent pruning or defoliation.
organic_control: Provide temporary partial shade net during extreme heat waves for young plants.
chemical_control: Not applicable.
cultural_practice: Avoid heavy pruning right before peak summer heat; maintain adequate soil moisture during heat waves.
prevention: Time pruning to avoid leaving canopy exposed during peak summer.
dosage_note: Not applicable.
expert_escalation_condition: If scorch is extensive and affecting overall plant vigor for multiple weeks.

symptoms: Irregular brown/scorched patches appearing shortly after a spray application, often uniform across recently sprayed leaves.
cause: Chemical phytotoxicity from incorrect dosage, spraying during high heat, or incompatible tank-mix.
favorable_weather: Hot, sunny conditions during/soon after spraying increase burn risk.
organic_control: Rinse foliage with plain water if burn is noticed immediately after spraying; avoid further chemical stress.
chemical_control: Discontinue the suspected product; consult local agriculture officer before resuming any spray.
cultural_practice: Always spray in early morning or evening, never at midday heat; follow correct dilution rates.
prevention: Read product labels fully, avoid mixing incompatible chemicals, calibrate sprayers correctly.
dosage_note: Always follow the exact label dosage - do not increase concentration to 'work faster'.
expert_escalation_condition: If burn is severe/widespread - consult agriculture officer before any further chemical application.
